newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rexrodt sees end to VW subsidies row.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt sees end to VW subsidies row.

text.p: Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Wednesday he believes the row with the European Union over 240 million marks ($159.3 million) in subsidies for auto maker Volkswagen AG will be resolved by year-end.

Rexrodt told journalists Germany has taken part in constructive negotiations with the EU. Kurt Biedenkopf, premier of the state of Saxony, which gave the subsidies to VW, is also optimistic a solution is near, Rexrodt said.
If the situation is resolved, Saxony will drop the complaint it has filed with the European Court of Justice.
The German government sees Saxony's actions as unacceptable, but it believes the subsidies are justified, Rexrodt said.
Bonn hopes the European Commission will recognise that Maastricht Treaty rules allowing subsidies to formerly communist east Germany are applicable in this case.
Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert warned last week the issue could heat up as year-end approaches.

A compromise struck with Bonn in September, neutralising 90 million marks in subsidies paid by Saxony despite Commission opposition, could be brought into question because Bonn had only committed itself to blocking an equivalent amount of authorised subsidies until the end of the year, Van Miert said.
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49 228 26097150 ($ = 1.506 German Marks)
